name: Question 9
problem: Suppose that a matrix $B$ has characteristic polynomial $p(\lambda )=(2-\lambda )^{3}(\lambda +\pi )^{15}(\lambda -1)^{4},$ the rank of $(B+\pi I)^{4}$ equals $8,$ and the rank of $(B+\pi I)^{3}$ equals $10.$ If a basis of ${R}^{22}$ consists of linearly independent generalized eigenvectors of $B$, how many of these are generalized eigenvectors of rank $4$ corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =-\pi ?$
worked_solution:
For the given matrix $B$ with eigenvalue $\lambda =-\pi ,$ a generalized eigenvector of rank $4$ is a vector $v$ such that 

$$
(B+\pi I)^{4}v=0\,\text{and}\,(B+\pi I)^{3}v\ne 0.
$$

Notice that $B$ must be a $22\times 22$ matrix.

- Since the rank of $(B+\pi I)^{3}$ equals $10,$ then by the rank-nullity theorem, we have that

$$
\text{nullity}(B+\pi I)^{3}=22-10=12.
$$

So, the solutions to $(B+\pi I)^{3}v=0$ form a subspace $\text{Null}(B+\pi I)^{3}$ of dimension $12$ in ${R}^{22}.$

- Since the rank of $(B+\pi I)^{4}$ equals $8,$  then by the rank-nullity theorem, we have that

$$
\text{nullity}(B+\pi I)^{4}=22-8=14.
$$

So, the solutions to $(B+\pi I)^{4}v=0$ form a subspace $\text{Null}(B+\pi I)^{4}$ of dimension $14$ in ${R}^{22}.$

Since $\text{Null}(B+\pi I)^{3}$ is a subspace of dimension $12$ in $\text{Null}(B+\pi I)^{4}$, which is a subspace of dimension $14,$ our basis can contain only $2$ vectors that lie in $\text{Null}(B+\pi I)^{4}$ but do not lie in $\text{Null}(B+\pi I)^{3}.$

Therefore, there will be 

$$
\text{nullity}(B+\pi I)^{4}-\text{nullity}(B+\pi I)^{3}=14-12=2
$$

 generalized eigenvectors of rank $4$ corresponding to the eigenvalue $\lambda =-\pi .$

Suppose that a matrix B has characteristic polynomial p(λ)=(2−λ)3(λ+π)15(λ−1)4, the rank of (B+πI)4 equals 8, and the rank of (B+πI)3 equals 10. If a basis of R22 consists of linearly independent generalized eigenvectors of B, how many of these are generalized eigenvectors of rank 4 corresponding to the eigenvalue λ=−π?

4

EXPLANATION

For the given matrix B with eigenvalue λ=−π, a generalized eigenvector of rank 4 is a vector v such that

(B+πI)4v=0and(B+πI)3v≠0.

Notice that B must be a 22×22 matrix.

  • Since the rank of (B+πI)3 equals 10, then by the rank-nullity theorem, we have that nullity(B+πI)3=22−10=12. So, the solutions to (B+πI)3v=0 form a subspace Null(B+πI)3 of dimension 12 in R22.

  • Since the rank of (B+πI)4 equals 8, then by the rank-nullity theorem, we have that nullity(B+πI)4=22−8=14. So, the solutions to (B+πI)4v=0 form a subspace Null(B+πI)4 of dimension 14 in R22.

Since Null(B+πI)3 is a subspace of dimension 12 in Null(B+πI)4, which is a subspace of dimension 14, our basis can contain only 2 vectors that lie in Null(B+πI)4 but do not lie in Null(B+πI)3.

Therefore, there will be nullity(B+πI)4−nullity(B+πI)3=14−12=2 generalized eigenvectors of rank 4 corresponding to the eigenvalue λ=−π.
